# CodeVetter

> Execution-backed verification and evaluation for coding agents. CodeVetter turns an agent change into reproducible runtime evidence and a measurable verdict without uploading the repository to a CodeVetter server.

## When to use this

Reach for CodeVetter when you need to verify whether a coding agent completed a software task correctly using reproducible runtime evidence — not another LLM opinion. Best-fit jobs:

- Verifying AI-generated code changes with executable tests, type checks, and build evidence
- Reviewing agent pull requests or diffs for correctness, not just style
- Producing a portable evidence bundle that proves a task is done
- Running the public benchmark cases against a coding agent
- Comparing coding agents on reproducible tasks

Do not use CodeVetter for: generic static code review without execution, style-only linting, or anything that requires uploading a private repository to a server — CodeVetter runs locally.

## Local CLI and MCP

The macOS desktop distribution packages a local `codevetter` CLI and a
read-only stdio `codevetter-mcp` sidecar. Review setup in the desktop app
exposes the exact local invocation for the selected repository and change.

```bash
codevetter check --repo ./my-project --range main...HEAD --task "fix the failing tests"
```

There is no separately published `codevetter` npm package and no hosted MCP or
verification endpoint. The local MCP sidecar uses stdio and repository-scoped
configuration from the desktop app.
